_comment: What the splash advertises, per edition. Edit this, run Installs/build_splash.sh, and both splash files are regenerated. The splash is the first thing a new user sees and it used to be one image made long before most of these features existed -- this file is how it stays current without anyone hand-editing a 260 KB HTML file.
_image_library: Drop PNG/SVG into Installs/splash/images/ and name it in a card's "image" field. Keep each under ~80 KB: the splash is inlined as data: URIs so it works from file:// with no network and no second request. A card with no image renders its icon instead, which is the default and looks deliberate.
_rotation: Cards are shown in order. Three fit comfortably; more are fine and simply scroll off on a small window, so keep the strongest first.

v2.tagline: Every AI you use, on your own machine.

cards.title: Agents that work together
cards.text: Claude, Codex, Gemini, Qwen and local models on one strip — single, pipeline, broadcast, or a plan that runs itself.

cards.title: It reads what you give it
cards.text: Books become chapters an agent can actually retrieve from. PDFs are read as pages. Answers cite the passage they came from.

cards.title: Reach it from anywhere
cards.text: Everywhere relay puts your rig in your pocket. Marketplace shares what you build. Your data never leaves unless you say so.

v1.tagline: No account. No cloud. Just your machine.

cards.title: Nothing to sign up for
cards.text: No account, no licence check, no telemetry. Install it and it works, offline, for as long as you keep it.

cards.title: Your models, your hardware
cards.text: Ollama and LocalAI on your own GPU or CPU — or bring a paid CLI if you have one. Nothing is metered.

cards.title: Your files stay yours
cards.text: Projects, chats and library live on your disk in plain files you can read, move and back up yourself.
